short: A single shot in a siege trench ended the reign, the war and the absolute monarchy.
full:
Charles XII invaded Norway in the autumn of 1718 and by late November was besieging the fortress of Fredriksten above Fredrikshald. On the evening of 11 December he was in a forward trench inspecting the approach works when a projectile struck him in the head and killed him instantly. The date is Gregorian; Sweden had returned to the Julian calendar in 1712, so Swedish tradition marks the day as 30 November.

Whether the shot came from the fortress or from among his own men has been argued ever since. The body was exhumed in 1746, 1859 and 1917 without settling the question, and the wound is consistent with either. The Norwegian campaign was abandoned within days. His sister Ulrika Eleonora obtained the throne only by accepting constitutional limits, and the Riksdag then wrote absolutism out of the constitution altogether, beginning the fifty-year Age of Liberty. Sabaton's "Long Live the King" is about the death and the reaction to it.
